title: Tax Laws Amendment (Implementation of the FATCA Agreement) Bill 2014
short_title: Tax Laws Amendment (Implementation of the FATCA Agreement) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would implement Australia's obligations under a tax information-sharing agreement with the United States.

Australian financial institutions would be required to provide the Tax Commissioner with details of accounts held by US taxpayers, which the Commissioner would then transmit to the US Internal Revenue Service.
The bill also sets up supporting rules for record-keeping, due diligence and transitional reporting on payments to non-participating financial institutions.
changes: Requires Australian financial institutions to report account information on US taxpayers to the Tax Commissioner.
Establishes record-keeping and due diligence duties for those institutions.
Creates transitional reporting obligations for payments to non-participating financial institutions.
summary.affected: Reporting Australian financial institutions and the Commissioner of Taxation.

speeches.speaker: Michael Sukkar
speeches.brief: Welcomed the FATCA agreement negotiated by Treasurer Joe Hockey, which spares Australian financial institutions a 30 per cent US withholding tax and requires reporting on US citizens with more than $50,000 in their accounts, and noted the government inherited a backlog of 96 unenacted tax and superannuation measures.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Giles
speeches.brief: Supported the FATCA bill while criticizing the government for forgoing more than $1 billion in revenue by not cracking down on multinational profit shifting, citing the 2009 case in which Swiss bank UBS paid US$780 million in fines for helping Americans evade tax, and estimated the US loses at least US$100 billion annually to offshore tax evasion.

speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: Defended the FATCA bill's $583 million compliance cost saving over 10 years, rejected Labor's amendment on multinational tax avoidance as a smokescreen for its proposed $38 billion to $40 billion in extra spending, and argued today's students will be repaying Labor's debt for 20 or 30 years.

speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: Summed up the tax bill, confirming the Medicare levy low-income threshold for families would rise from $33,693 to $34,367, and said overall share trading activity had grown 5 per cent since the 'distribution washing' crackdown was announced, with no support for the opposition's amendment.
